messages:
anya: Intake: customer Delta asks for a concise safety checklist + rollout acceptance for tenant-level model swaps (quantized variants). Main ask: no visible quality regressions and predictable p95 latency.
leo: Problem summary: some tenants experience output drift after model switch. They want an auditable gate + automated fallback.
anya: Goals: (1) define numeric acceptance gates, (2) provide an uploadable eval bundle API, (3) runtime canary controller + instant rollback, (4) Console summary for per-tenant rollout state.
rachel: Non-goals: retraining, global autoscaling changes, advanced model surgery. Keep v1 to server-side checks, UI visibility, and runbook.
tom: Acceptance gate suggestions: p95 latency cap, relative quality delta on tenant eval bundle, and a simple hallucination heuristic. Also require minimum eval size.
leo: Proposal: p95 <= 300ms; quality regression <= 3% relative; hallucination increase <= 1%. Minimum eval prompts = 25 for auto-rollout; otherwise flag manual review.
anya: Sampling and rollback: sampling window = 5min, require 3 consecutive windows breach -> auto-rollback (15min). Canary seq: 5% 30m -> 25% 90m -> 100%. Include kill-switch.
rachel: Eval bundle: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/evals {name, prompts[], answers[]}. Managed storage by default; optional S3 link. Keep retention 90 days with export.
tom: Edge cases: tiny eval sets, bursts of traffic skewing latency, and incompatible tokenizers between variants. Add compatibility check pre-rollout.
leo: Console needs a compact timeline + top 5 failing prompts + quick revert button. Also surface confidence level when eval size small.
anya: Ownership (quick): eng-data: metric definitions; eng-runtime: canary controller + fallback; frontend/design: Console; prod-ops: eval API & storage; SRE: runbook + SLOs.
rachel: Success metrics: reduce regression reports by 80%; median rollback recovery < 10min; 70% pilot self-serve within two days.
ops-bot: scheduled staging window: 2024-11-15T10:00Z (2h). Reminder 30m prior.
anya: Next step: I'll draft PRD with these numbers and share for review by Wed. Any objections to this scope?
leo: none.
rachel: good.
tom: ok.
anya: thanks — dropping PRD in #product when ready.
